fields.corePath: GST Saathi is for gig workers — Swiggy riders, Urban Company partners, freelance designers — who have crossed the registration threshold and have no idea what to do next. Users can manage their income entries from all their platforms in one place. They can also handle their expense claims and see what is deductible. The app supports quarterly return preparation and gives users visibility into their liability. There is a document vault where users can keep their invoices organised. Users can also access reminders so that they never miss a filing date, and there is a section where they can understand the rules in simple Hindi and English. Overall the product lets a gig worker take control of their GST compliance without hiring a CA at ₹2,000 a month.
fields.knownGaps: The Hindi content is machine translated for now and a CA friend has agreed to review it once he is out of tax audit season, so until then I would not fully trust the Hindi wording on the deduction pages. Some of the deduction rules are simplified — I have collapsed a few of the composition-scheme cases into one rule because explaining all of them to a rider is not useful. We are still working on the actual return filing: right now it prepares the numbers but you take them to the GST portal yourself and key them in, which is honestly the annoying half. The platform connections are one-way reads and only Swiggy has been tested against a real account, the others I built against sample statements a friend sent me. Bill photographs over about 4 MB fail silently on upload. The reminder emails go out at 9 am IST fixed, no timezone handling, which is fine for now since everyone is in India.
